newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan firm drums up subscribers for flotation.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan firm drums up subscribers for flotation.

text.p: Moroccan leasing firm Maroc-Leasing has launched a nation-wide advertisement campaign to drum up subscribers for a flotation on the Casablanca stock exchange, a Bourse official said on Wednesday.

The firm said it wanted to increase its capital by 21 percent to 106 million dirhams ($11.5 million). The floatation is expected to take place between 17 to 21 February 1997, the official said. One lot of 212,660 shares will be sold to the public at 230 dirhams per share from 17 to 21 of February, 1997, the official said.
But 1.0 percent of the increase will be devoted to company's employees, he added.

Maroc-Leasing said a tranche of 106,330 shares, or 10 percent, of the capital, would be reserved to local and foreign investors including institutions. The second tranche of 106,330 shares would be devoted to mutual funds.
The minimum subscription was set a five shares for the public and private investors and 1,000 shares for mutual funds, the firm said.
Established in Casablanca in 1965, Maroc-Leasing now has a capital of 84 million shares.
Morocco's second largest conglomerate Societe Nationale d'Investissement and Banque Nationale pour le Developpement Economique hold respectively 35 and 65 percent of the firm's stock.
The firm showed a net profit of 8.68 million dirhams in the first nine months of 1996 against 18.1 million dirhams for the whole year of 1995.
Maroc-Leasing expects a net profit of 14.9 million dirhams in 1996, officials said.
It is the second private firm to be floated on the bourse, after credit firm Credor, since the market reform programme was launched by the government in 1993.
Maroc-Leasing is expected to be listed on the Casablanca stock exchange on February 27, 1997. ($1= 9.2 dirhams)
